name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This lets us measure its impact without risking live changes. The trade-off is temporary noise in review data, but we gain real-world evidence before committing. If the data shows value, we scale it up; if not, we drop it. No safer way to test.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode risks training reviewers to ignore *all* autofeedback—not just noise—because the signal is indistinguishable from the noise. A better alternative is to run PR-Agent in shadow mode *only on merged PRs* for two weeks, then compare review quality metrics (e.g., review depth, time-to-merge) against a control period. If the merged PRs show no measurable improvement, the experiment fails; if they do, we scale to open PRs.
